checks.engine_answer: Yes, in one case. A 'destroy a node' harm never takes your last node, and neither does Siege's node loss. But Overrun (tier 2) corrupts the uncorrupted city its token is on, and corruption destroys any node on that hex. Only the stage-I last-node rule guards that, so from stage II on it can take your last node, unless Shelter, hardening, your ambassador, Aegis or Sanctuary saves it. Casus Belli's extra war step next round can also take a last node on a factory that war destroys.

checks.engine_answer: Usually yes. Deploy lands on the lowest-numbered factory of any owner, skipping a hex with the Protector's node. In the same turn's march the troop's first step strikes a target on or next to its hex; if there are several, the players choose which, so it may hit a neighbor instead. Stoppers in order: Shelter, a corp troop at a base on or next to the hex (it is removed), a hardening token, the factory owner's ambassador, Aegis. The troop is used up either way. Shelter can't actually be up then: it is set in the action phase and falls at cleanup. If corruption earlier in the turn took the factory, it is no longer a target.
